questions.q: In the lesson's example, why does the "environment" variable have no default?
options: Because variables are never allowed to have defaults
Because its value must be supplied every run, since Terraform has no sensible fallback for it
Because it isn't a string type
Because outputs can't reference variables without defaults
questions.explain: A variable with no default is required — Terraform will refuse to run until a value is supplied, since there's no safe assumption for something like environment.

questions.q: How do you reference a declared variable named vm_size elsewhere in your configuration?
options: vm_size by itself
${vm_size}
var.vm_size
input.vm_size
questions.explain: A declared variable is referenced anywhere in the configuration as var.<name>, such as var.vm_size.

questions.q: What happens if a file is named exactly terraform.tfvars?
options: It is ignored unless explicitly deleted
Terraform loads it automatically, with no -var-file flag needed
It overrides every resource block in the configuration
It must be renamed before terraform apply will run
questions.explain: A file named exactly terraform.tfvars is loaded automatically. Teams that keep multiple environment-specific files instead pass the right one explicitly with -var-file.

questions.q: Why might an output value, like a storage account's endpoint, only be knowable after terraform apply runs?
options: Because output blocks are evaluated before any resource exists
Because that value is generated by the cloud provider when the resource is actually created, and doesn't exist in the .tf files beforehand
Because outputs can only reference variables, never resources
Because Terraform deletes resource attributes after apply
questions.explain: Some attributes, like a storage account's primary endpoint, are assigned by the provider at creation time and simply don't exist until the resource is actually provisioned.

questions.q: What does running `terraform output resource_group_name` do?
options: Deletes the resource_group_name output
Prints only that one output's current value
Re-runs terraform apply for that resource only
Renames the resource group
questions.explain: Passing a specific output name to terraform output prints just that value — exactly what a script would use to pull a single value out programmatically.
